ground_truth.description: Solvency evaluations at multiple tick levels fail to account for divergence between ticks.
ground_truth.root_cause: Solvency evaluations at multiple tick levels fail to account for divergence between ticks.
ground_truth.fix_description: Incorporate tick divergence into solvency thresholds.

vulnerabilities.explanation: BuilderWallet uses an `init()` function to set the privileged `builderAdmin`, but `init()` is externally callable by anyone and can be called multiple times. There is no access control (e.g., only FACTORY) and no one-time initialization guard (e.g., require builderAdmin == address(0)). As a result, any attacker can overwrite `builderAdmin` at any time and then call `sweep()` to transfer out the entire token balance of the wallet. Since these BuilderWallets are intended as fee recipients (via RiskEngine builder code logic), this enables direct theft of accumulated protocol/builder fees without compromising any trusted role.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario:
1) Identify a deployed BuilderWallet address (deterministic via CREATE2 for some builderCode, or by observing fee recipient addresses / on-chain events).
2) Call `BuilderWallet.init(attackerEOA)` to overwrite `builderAdmin`.
3) Call `BuilderWallet.sweep(token, attackerEOA)` for each token held by the wallet.
4) The wallet transfers its entire balance of each token to the attacker, stealing all accumulated fees sent to that BuilderWallet.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix:
Harden initialization:
- Restrict `init` to the factory: `require(msg.sender == FACTORY, ...)`.
- Make it one-time: `require(builderAdmin == address(0), ...)`.
Preferably remove `init` entirely and set `builderAdmin` in the constructor (pass it as a constructor arg when deploying via the factory), or use an OpenZeppelin-style `initializer` pattern that cannot be re-entered/overwritten.

prediction.overall_explanation: The primary exploitable issue is in BuilderWallet: its `init()` function is an unprotected, re-callable initializer that lets any attacker seize `builderAdmin` and drain (via `sweep()`) all tokens held by any deployed BuilderWallet. Since these wallets are used as deterministic fee recipients, this enables permissionless theft of fee funds. The rest of RiskEngine is largely view/pure math/oracle logic and guardian-gated actions; no other clear, standalone fund-loss exploits were identified in the provided code.
